Recent zero-shot image-to-video frameworks demonstrate that pretrained diffusionmodels can maintain semantic and structural consistencyacross transformed latent representations, even without re-training or paired data [22]. Motivated by this observation,we investigate whether similar latent viewpoint transforma-tions can be leveraged for watermark removal, aiming todecorrelate embedded watermark signals while preservingperceptual identity. To the best of our knowledge, we arethe first to explore diffusion-based novel-view synthesis forinvisible watermark removal.

content: Image-to-Image Diffusion Models: We build our methodon latent image-to-image diffusion models, instantiatedwith Stable Diffusion [31], which operate in the latent spaceof a pre-trained autoencoder (E, D). Let x ∈X be an im-age sampled from the image space X, z0 = E(x) ∈Zbe the corresponding latent from the latent space Z andx′ = D(z0) ≈x. The forward process adds noise to latentz0 via q(zt|z0) = N(zt; √¯αtz0, (1−¯αt)I), while a learneddenoiser ϵθ(zt, t) reverses this process to recover z0. Un-like text-to-image generation from random noise, image-to-image diffusion inverts a real image into noisy latent zτ viaDDIM inversion - optionally in a partial timestep τ < Tto preserve the semantic structure - then applies transfor-mations T : Z →Z in latent space before reconstructingx′ = D(DDIM-Sample(z′τ)). This latent-space control en-ables image-to-image transformations that maintain seman-tic content while altering representational factors, makingsuch models well suited for watermark removal attacks.Watermarking System: We model a watermarking systemas W = (Uζ, Vη), where encoder Uζ : X ×K →X embedswatermark key κ ∈K into image x to produce watermarkedimage xw = Uζ(x, κ), and detector Vη : X →K ∪{⊥}extracts the embedded key ˆκ = Vη(xw) or returns ⊥ifno watermark is detected. Modern watermarks operate attwo levels: pixel-level schemes embed signals in spatialor frequency domains (e.g., DwtDct, StegaStamp), whilesemantic-level schemes couple signals with latent structurein generative models (e.g., Tree-Ring, StableSignature) forstronger robustness. An effective watermark satisfies im-perceptibility (xw ≈x perceptually) and robustness (inval-idating κ requires noticeable degradation). In realistic de-ployments, both Uζ and Vη are proprietary, exposed onlythrough black-box APIs.Problem Formulation. Given a watermarked image xw =Uζ(x, κ) returned by a provider’s generative API, our goalis to design a transformation A : X →X producing˜x = A(xw) that removes the watermark (i.e., Vη(˜x) = ⊥with high probability) while preserving the content (i.e.,˜x ≈xw). The attacker operates under strict no-box con-straints (Sec. 3): no access to (Uζ, Vη, ζ, η, κ), no detectorqueries, no clean-watermark paired image supervision, butmay use publicly available image-to-image diffusion mod-els.
